_comment: Stories: pre-written chains of events with acts and endings (scripts/events.gd, events in data/events/stories.json). An event with "story" and "act" moves its story on; "ending STORY KEY" closes it; a chain that runs out goes cold. At most rules.events.max_stories run at once. acts: names, shown in the log. endings: {name, text}; text can use the story's roles. boost: while it's open, these events are this many times likelier. repeat: it can be told again once it ends.

brother.title: A Brother's Knife
brother.summary: You sacked {town}. {avenger} lost a brother there, and means to make you pay for it.

killed.name: Settled with steel
killed.text: {avenger} died on the beach below {town}. The town buried them next to their brother.

murdered.name: Settled with grape
murdered.text: Your gunners settled it from the boat. {town} will tell that story for a hundred years.

forgiven.name: Forgiven, in a way
forgiven.text: {avenger} took your money for the church roof. Forgiven is too strong a word. But it's over.

spared_you.name: Spared
spared_you.text: {avenger} had you on the sand with a blade at your throat, and let you live. You don't know what to do with that.

avenged.name: Avenged
avenged.text: {avenger} watched you beaten and dragged into port, and that was enough. They went home.

silver.title: The Old Man's Silver
silver.summary: A dying buccaneer told you of Panama silver buried on a cay off {port}. Someone else was listening.

passed_by.name: Let it lie
passed_by.text: You never went to the cay. Perhaps the silver is still there.

let_go.name: Let it go
let_go.text: {listener} got the old man's silver. You got a story to tell.

found.name: Silver from Panama
found.text: The old man's silver came aboard at last, in a stranger's hold.

lost.name: Outrun
lost.text: {listener}'s friends got away with the rest of the silver.

debt.title: The Debt
debt.summary: {who} owes money in {town}, and the people they owe it to don't forget.

paid.name: Paid
paid.text: The ledger is clean. {who} won't forget who cleaned it.

paid_dear.name: Paid, dearly
paid_dear.text: Twice what it was. But {who} is free of it.

handed_over.name: Handed over
handed_over.text: {who} went to the debtors' prison. The crew remember.

taken.name: Taken in the night
taken.text: They came for {who} in the night, and nobody stopped them.

burned.name: The ledger burned
burned.text: No ledger, no debt. {town} won't love you for it.

bargain.name: A bargain struck
bargain.text: {who}'s debt is the ship's debt now, paid from the next voyages.

castaway.title: The Castaway
castaway.summary: You marooned {who}. They didn't die on the sandbar.

reconciled.name: Amends
reconciled.text: You found {who} and paid what it was worth. Neither of you will call it friendship.

returned.name: Back aboard
returned.text: {who} took their old berth back. The crew watch them, and you, very carefully.

hanged.name: Hanged
hanged.text: You hanged {who} from your own yardarm. Nobody aboard said a word.

marooned_again.name: Marooned again
marooned_again.text: {who} went back to a sandbar, with a pistol and one ball this time.

even.name: Even
even.text: You let {who} go. You're even, the two of you, or near enough.

escaped.name: Still out there
escaped.text: {who} is out there still, and knows your ship better than you do.

pardon.title: The Pardon
pardon.summary: You took the King's pardon. {friend}, who sailed on the account with you, didn't.

warned.name: A word of warning
warned.text: You warned {friend}. The governor will hear of it, sooner or later.

refused.name: Not that
refused.text: You turned down the commission. Pardoned men aren't supposed to say no.

let_slip.name: Lost in the fog
let_slip.text: You let {friend} slip away and reported that you'd lost them. Nobody believed you.

delivered.name: Delivered
delivered.text: {friend} hanged at the next assizes. You were paid in full.

freed.name: A cut rope
freed.text: Somebody cut {friend}'s bonds in the night. The governor has a good idea who.

escaped.name: Away
escaped.text: {friend} got away, and won't forgive you for coming after them.

warrant.title: The Warrant
warrant.summary: Captain {hunter}, the lieutenant you locked in the cable tier, has a warrant for mutiny with your name on it.

understood.name: Torn in half
understood.text: {hunter} heard the truth and tore up the warrant. You still don't know why you told it.

bought.name: Bought and paid for
bought.text: {hunter} had debts. The warrant went into the fire with the receipt.

killed.name: Settled in an alley
killed.text: {hunter} died in an alley in the islands. The navy will send someone else, someday.

hanged.name: From your yardarm
hanged.text: You hanged {hunter} from your own yardarm, and {nation} will never forget it.

spared.name: Spared
spared.text: You put {hunter} ashore with their sword. Neither of you knows what that settled.

dead_on_paper.name: Dead on paper
dead_on_paper.text: {hunter} wrote home that you drowned. Officially, you did.

beaten.name: Next time, a rope
beaten.text: {hunter} beat you, took your colours and let you go. Next time, a rope.

cold.name: Still out there
cold.text: {hunter} stopped turning up. The warrant didn't stop being true.

brand.title: The Mark
brand.summary: {master} still holds your indenture: years left to serve, and a runaway's mark on your shoulder to say whose they are.

freed.name: Irons over the side
freed.text: You freed a ship bound for {master}'s fields, and some of them chose to sail with you.

landed.name: Where they asked
landed.text: You took the people from {master}'s slaver where they asked to go. {master} lost a fortune and gained an enemy.

failed.name: Beaten off
failed.text: You tried to take {master}'s slaver, and failed. There's a price on your head for trying.

defied.name: Ashes
defied.text: You burned {master}'s letter in front of {master}'s lawyer. The warrants are still being bought.

bought.name: Papers
bought.text: You bought out your own indenture from a clerk in {town}. It shouldn't have cost anything.

threatened.name: One day
threatened.text: You wrote to {master} that you'd come for them one day. {master} hasn't slept well since.

cold.name: Still marked
cold.text: {master} went quiet. The mark on your shoulder didn't.

partner.title: Who Took the Blame
partner.summary: {partner} held the quay the night you got away. Now they wait for a rope in the gaol at {town}.

freed.name: A key after all
freed.text: You bought {partner} out of the gaol at {town}. They sail with you now.

broke_out.name: Over the wall
broke_out.text: You broke {partner} out of the gaol at {town} in the night. {town} hasn't forgiven it.

pardoned.name: Through the front door
pardoned.text: You talked the governor of {town} round, and {partner} walked out free.

lawyer.name: A good lawyer
lawyer.text: You sent a lawyer instead of yourself. You never heard what happened.

hanged.name: Too late
hanged.text: You tried to break {partner} out, and failed. They hanged the next morning.

abandoned.name: Not your problem
abandoned.text: You left {partner} to hang in {town} for what you did.

cold.name: Somewhere else
cold.text: {partner} hanged in {town} on a grey morning. You were somewhere else.

promise.title: A Lamp in the Window
promise.summary: You promised {dear}, in {town}, that you'd come back. They're still waiting.

house.name: The house on the hill
house.text: There's a house on the hill above {town}, with {dear} and a lamp in the window.

aboard.name: Aboard
aboard.text: {dear} sails with you now. Some promises you keep by changing them.

released.name: Don't wait
released.text: You told {dear} not to wait. They didn't.

married.name: Married a chandler
married.text: {dear} married a chandler in {town}. They wished you well, and meant it.

cold.name: The lamp went out
cold.text: You never went back to {town}. Eventually, {dear} stopped lighting the lamp.
